EXTEND C0004 | FIND: `scan_health()` only inserts keys into `tools_available` for runners it attempts, and when `source_paths` has no existing files it returns `HealthScan(...)` with the default empty dict. The report therefore omits tool state entirely instead of emitting explicit false/unavailable status for pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy. Evidence: `if not existing: return HealthScan(...)`; otherwise the loop populates only attempted tool names. FOLLOW: downstream consumers cannot distinguish “all tools unavailable / nothing scanned” from “field absent because endocrine forgot to report status”, which makes the health monitor’s availability contract non-total and can mislead insect-brain/human review on infrastructure health. This is the same root cause family as misreported availability: tool-status reporting is incomplete. FIX: initialize `tools_available` with all expected tool names set to `False`, then overwrite per tool as execution status becomes known, including the no-existing-files path.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually run tests against the patched source tree. It writes only the patched target file into a temp dir, then executes `test_cmd` unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. The command still points at the original test paths/module names, and the rest of the source tree is not copied into the sandbox. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no project tree copy occurs; `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)` runs the caller-provided command verbatim. In the actual immune integration, `evaluate_fixes()` is invoked with `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which from inside the temp dir resolves to the real repo tests/imports, not a sandboxed patched checkout.
FOLLOW: This breaks the key “fix evaluation” capability in two ways before any fix is proposed. First, tests can silently validate the unmodified real code instead of the patched candidate, producing false SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts for fixes that would fail if actually exercised. Second, if tests import modules from the real repo while static checks run on the temp file, endocrine compares mixed environments: lint/type counts from sandbox, behavior from production tree. That makes `verified=True` propagation in the immune pipeline unsound, so bad fixes can be marked verified, causing NK bug-closed gating to suppress future findings on still-broken bugs.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the whole project context, not just one file: create a temp workspace containing a copy of the repo subtree needed by `test_cmd`, replace the target file at its original relative path inside that workspace, and run both static tools and tests against that workspace so all evaluation happens on one patched tree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — even apart from tests, `evaluate_fix()` runs pyright/ruff/bandit on a standalone temp file path that has lost its original project location and neighboring modules. Evidence: the patched file is written to `tmpdir / basename(target_path)`, not to the original relative path inside a copied tree. `run_pyright([patched_path])`, `run_ruff([patched_path])`, and `run_bandit([patched_path])` therefore analyze an isolated file with different import resolution, config discovery, and package context than the original file. Any same-basename collision from different directories is also erased.
FOLLOW: Fix verdicts become mechanically wrong in both directions. A safe patch may be marked HARMFUL because imports/configs disappear in the temp root; a harmful patch may be marked SAFE because tool configuration rooted in the real project no longer applies. Since immune stage 4 treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as programmatic verification, this interface error feeds directly into verified/escalated state and duplicate closure logic. It undermines end-to-end trust in endocrine’s core purpose: “does the proposed fix break anything?”
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — preserve original relative paths and project context during sandbox evaluation: copy the relevant source tree/config into the temp dir, write the patch back to the file’s original relative path there, and invoke tools with `cwd` set to that sandbox root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` judges harm by summing net issue deltas across tools: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit; if total_net > 0: HARMFUL; if total_net < 0: SAFE`. This allows one tool’s improvement to cancel another tool’s regression. Example from the current logic: `-3 ruff, +1 pyright, +1 bandit` yields `-1` and is marked SAFE despite introducing a new type error and a new security issue.
FOLLOW: Downstream, endocrine can certify regressions as SAFE/NEUTRAL, which then marks findings `verified=True` in the immune pipeline. That can close bugs even when the proposed fix introduces a new correctness or security defect. For PoC this is HIGH because it silently produces wrong verification verdicts rather than merely degrading scoring.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive or tests fail; only classify as SAFE when no metric regresses and at least one improves or tests pass. Do not let improvements in one tool offset regressions in another.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.37
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A mention like `brain.py` will match any path containing that substring, and a basename found in prose/proposed_fix can resolve to the first incidental containing path rather than the intended source file. The regex also scrapes every `*.py` token from both description and fix text without prioritizing exact path matches.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` may patch and analyze the wrong file while still returning a normal verdict. That yields false UNEVALUABLE, false SAFE, or false HARMFUL outcomes disconnected from the finding under review. Because the result is keyed only by `finding_id`, the immune pipeline can mark the original finding verified based on analysis of an unrelated file.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve target files by exact normalized basename/relative-path match only: first prefer exact full-path matches against `source_paths`, then unique basename matches, and return UNEVALUABLE on ambiguity instead of using substring containment.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source()` whole-file replacement accepts any syntactically valid Python text with at least 5 newlines, regardless of whether it resembles a complete file or corresponds to the described fix. The comment says it only applies replacements that “start with import or def or class”, but the implementation does not enforce that check. Evidence: after `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")`, the only gate is `if fix.count("\n") >= 5: return fix`.
FOLLOW: Natural-language fix prose that happens to compile, partial snippets, or unrelated multi-line code blocks can replace the entire source file. That creates spurious HARMFUL/SAFE verdicts driven by an over-permissive patch applicator rather than by the proposed fix. Since endocrine’s evaluation result is later used as programmatic verification, this can misclassify findings and close bugs on the basis of an accidentally swapped-in file body.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make whole-file replacement opt-in and strict: only return `fix` when it is valid Python and clearly marked as a complete replacement, e.g. starts with a file-level construct after stripping (`import`, `from`, `class`, `def`, module docstring) and contains no explanatory prose markers; otherwise fall through to UNEVALUABLE.
VERIFIED: TRUE
